Survey design and weighting

Source: vignettes/articles/survey-design.Rmd
survey-design.Rmd

Build the cohort design

nis_design() validates YEAR, HOSP_NIS, NIS_STRATUM, and DISCWT, then constructs a survey design before applying the declared domain. Existing dplyr groups (including rowwise grouping) are removed first, for both data frames and lazy DuckDB queries. Aggregate cohort expressions such as LOS > mean(LOS) use the full input rather than each input group. To use a group-specific threshold, compute an explicit cohort indicator upstream and pass that column to cohort. Group the returned survey design when you need grouped survey summaries.

nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019:2020)) |>
  nis_flag_dx(heart_failure = "I50")
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/Rtmp2XOGhO/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/Rtmp2XOGhO/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
design <- nis_design(
  nis,
  cohort = heart_failure & AGE >= 18,
  keep = c(AGE, LOS),
  annualize = TRUE
)
#> Preparing the cohort survey design.
srvyr::summarise(design, total = srvyr::survey_total(),
                 mean_los = srvyr::survey_mean(LOS))
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>   total total_se mean_los mean_los_se
#>   <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1  62.4     8.67     5.66       0.229

The output contains a weighted fixture total and mean LOS with design-based standard errors. Hospital placeholders account for hospital-years with no cohort discharges in the variance calculation. The returned design exposes only cohort discharges to summaries. This placeholder strategy is experimental.

For lazy inputs, DuckDB computes hospital-year strata, invalid-field counts, and annualization coverage in one sample scan. The separate cohort scan collects the selected columns needed to build the survey design in R.

Analyze a domain within the cohort

The object returned by nis_design() is already an srvyr survey design. Use dplyr::filter() on that object to define an analytic domain. Like subset() on a survey design, it uses the original sampling structure for variance. Hospitals with no domain discharges contribute zero, including when an entire stratum falls outside the domain.

On the design returned by nis_design(), filter() also removes out-of-domain records from the stored analysis data. The survey design retains the original sampled hospital counts for variance estimation, so there is no separate compaction step. If you no longer need the wider design, assign the filtered result back to the same variable.

design |>
  dplyr::filter(AGE >= 65) |>
  dplyr::group_by(YEAR) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    mean_los = srvyr::survey_mean(LOS),
    discharges = srvyr::unweighted(dplyr::n())
  )
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>    YEAR mean_los mean_los_se discharges
#>   <int>    <dbl>       <dbl>      <int>
#> 1  2019     5.11       0.606         22
#> 2  2020     5.11       0.606         22

discharges counts only observed domain discharges. The filtered design can also be passed directly to survey functions and to gtsummary::tbl_svysummary().

Filtering the lazy input before nis_design() restricts the records available to construct the design and can remove entire hospitals or strata. To define a cohort within the available sample, pass the inclusion criteria to cohort. To narrow an existing design to a subpopulation, filter the returned design.

Choose a pooling convention

Without annualization, pooled-year weights represent the combined included period. annualize = TRUE divides by the number of valid years; partial years count as a year. When quarter fields are present the function warns about incomplete year coverage and a 2015 cohort restricted to one coding era. Exclude partial years or choose a documented alternative if this convention does not fit the estimand.

Run a weighted sensitivity analysis

Use the original survey design for national totals. The example below compares the original mean LOS difference with one weighted to balance the observed age distribution between groups. It uses invented data and targets the age distribution of the pooled adult discharge population. The propensity model uses age as its only predictor.

original <- nis_design(nis, AGE >= 18, keep = c(AGE, LOS, heart_failure))
#> Preparing the cohort survey design.
propensity <- survey::svyglm(
  heart_failure ~ AGE, design = original, family = quasibinomial()
)
p <- stats::predict(propensity, newdata = original$variables, type = "response")
stopifnot(all(is.finite(p) & p > 0 & p < 1))

weighted <- nis_reweight(original, ifelse(heart_failure, 1 / p, 1 / (1 - p)))
age_by_group <- function(design) {
  survey::svyby(~AGE, ~heart_failure, design, survey::svymean)
}
los_contrast <- function(design) {
  fit <- survey::svyglm(LOS ~ heart_failure, design)
  summary(fit)$coefficients["heart_failureTRUE", c("Estimate", "Std. Error")]
}

age_by_group(original)
#>       heart_failure      AGE        se
#> FALSE         FALSE 62.04231 1.2732597
#> TRUE           TRUE 57.55769 0.9866784
age_by_group(weighted)
#>       heart_failure      AGE        se
#> FALSE         FALSE 59.63008 1.4907428
#> TRUE           TRUE 59.63404 0.9660242
rbind(original = los_contrast(original), reweighted = los_contrast(weighted))
#>             Estimate Std. Error
#> original   0.2826923  0.4126637
#> reweighted 0.1555133  0.4113503
srvyr::summarise(original, national_discharges = srvyr::survey_total())
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   national_discharges national_discharges_se
#>                 <dbl>                  <dbl>
#> 1                229.                   5.66

nis_reweight() is experimental. It multiplies the survey weights by the supplied factors, in the order of the design rows. The weighted mean contrast and its standard error use that transformed design. This variance treats the supplied factors as fixed. Report the propensity specification, weight range, any trimming or exclusions, and balance in the variables used to justify the sensitivity analysis. The age means illustrate one balance check. The example uses all weights without trimming. Causal interpretation would require a justified exposure definition, target population, and assumptions about confounding and overlap.

Why design-based standard errors matter

NIS uses hospital clusters, strata, and discharge weights. Ordinary means and standard errors treat rows as if they came from a simple random sample and do not reflect that structure. Use srvyr or survey methods on the returned design for point estimates and uncertainty. A survey standard error is an estimate of sampling variability under the supplied design, not a guarantee that all sources of bias have been addressed.

Inspect exclusions

Rows with missing, non-finite, or non-positive design fields are excluded before the cohort is applied. Inspect the aggregate audit attribute and report the exclusions with the analysis.

attr(design, "nis_excluded")
#> $total
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $by_field
#>        YEAR    HOSP_NIS NIS_STRATUM      DISCWT 
#>           0           0           0           0 
#> 
#> $by_year
#> # A tibble: 0 × 2
#> # ℹ 2 variables: YEAR <int>, n <dbl>

This list gives counts by field and year, not record-level information.

Common pitfalls

Common pitfalls

  • Treating annualized weights as a correction for arbitrary partial-year coverage.
  • Using non-survey summaries for estimates or uncertainty.
  • Treating reweighting or placeholder-row variance methods as established methods; both are experimental.

See nis_design(), nis_reweight(), and Data notes by year.
